slides.headline: 5 GOVERNMENT AI RULES QUIETLY COSTING YOU HOURS

caption:
The UK government just published 5 official AI rules for workers. Every one says to use it less. 📋

1) Ask if you really need AI first.
Flip it: "What would AI do first on my list today?"

2) Check if a spreadsheet can do it.
Real move: "Here's my data. What would a human take 2 hours to find?"

3) Use the worst model to save energy.
This one gets me. "What am I missing about this decision?" Use the best free model.

4) Keep prompts short for the planet.
More context wins: "Full context: [your situation]. What would an expert do?"

5) Use AI only when necessary.
Their whole point. "Run my weekly report. Where do I sign off?"

SAVE THIS: 5 government rules, 5 prompts that flip them.

Every government is writing AI rules right now. Most are written by people who have never used it seriously. The gap between official guidance and what actually works is growing. Close that gap and you stay ahead.

pinned_comment: Which rule gets you the most? Number 3 is the one I genuinely cannot get over.

hook_tournament.why: [4] hits harder because 'worth ignoring' is bolder than 'nobody will follow'—it's active dismissal, not prediction. The contradiction (official rules / ignore them) creates instant 'wait, WHAT?' tension that makes you stop scrolling to find out why.

candidates: 5 AI RULES MOST PEOPLE FOLLOW BLINDLY AND LOSE HOURS
5 GOVERNMENT AI RULES QUIETLY COSTING YOU HOURS
hook_sharpen.why: It tells you something's secretly costing you time right now—way more urgent than being told rules are worth ignoring. Personal threats at 2am hit harder than any advice.
